title: Passengers, Cargo & Groups
summary: How to prepare for and ride safely with a passenger or a load, and how to ride as part of a group.

sections.heading: Before you carry a passenger or load

blocks.text: Extra weight changes how a motorcycle handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers or large loads, and the bike needs adjusting first.

items: Tire pressure: check both tires against the owner's manual or the label on the bike. Most of the weight goes on the rear, but do not skip the front.
Suspension: with a heavy load you may need to adjust settings such as spring preload to make up for the lowered rear.
Weight limit: with cargo and a passenger, never exceed the motorcycle's gross vehicle weight rating.
Before loading, park about 10 feet from a wall in a dark garage and mark where the headlight beam hits.
Load up with your passenger and cargo, then check the beam again.
If it now hits higher, use the headlight's adjusting screws to lower it to the original mark.
Your passenger wears the same level of protective gear as you.
The motorcycle has passenger footrests.
The seat is big enough for two without crowding. You should not have to sit farther forward than usual.
There is a strap or solid handholds for the passenger.
Children sit immediately behind the rider. A child in front cannot balance properly and may interfere with your control.

blocks.text: Never assume a passenger knows how a motorcycle handles. Go over the basics before every trip, even if your passenger rides too. Tell them to:

items: Get on only after you have started the engine and shifted to neutral. While they mount, keep both your feet down and the front brake on.
Sit as far forward as possible without getting in the way of your control.
Hold firmly to your waist, hips or belt, or the passenger handholds.
Keep both feet on the footrests, even when stopped, so they do not fall off and pull you off.
Keep legs away from mufflers, chains and moving parts.
Stay directly behind you and lean with you in turns and curves. Looking over your shoulder toward the turn helps.
Avoid needless talking, leaning or turning around, and make no sudden moves.
Rise slightly off the seat when crossing an obstacle.

blocks.text: Remind your passenger to tighten their hold when you approach bumps or rough pavement, start from a stop or move into traffic, or are about to turn sharply or make a sudden move.
The heavier the passenger, the longer it may take to speed up, slow down or turn.

items: Ride a little slower, especially in curves, corners and over bumps. If any part of the bike scrapes the ground while leaned, you can lose steering control.
Start slowing earlier for stops and keep a larger space cushion whenever you slow or stop.
Wait for bigger gaps before you cross, enter or merge into traffic.

rows: Over or in front of the rear axle. Loads behind it affect turning and braking and can cause a wobble.
Keep loads low or in saddlebags. A high load raises the center of gravity and can upset balance.
Put about the same weight in each. An uneven load makes the bike pull to one side. Overloading can let a bag catch in the wheel or chain.
Use elastic cords or nets with more than one attachment point per side. Rope stretches and knots loosen. Stop often to check the load.
Mount it securely so it does not block your view of the controls or catch brake lines or cables.

blocks.text: Before a trip, test ride the fully loaded bike on familiar roads. Expect slower acceleration, which means longer passing times and distances, and braking that feels different, with possibly longer stopping distances. Make sure nothing scrapes in turns or over bumps.

items: Ride alert and free of alcohol and drugs, with the bike checked before you leave.
Hold a rider's meeting about the route, riding segments, rest stops, fuel, meals and lodging. If everyone knows the route, a separated rider will not have to hurry to keep from getting lost.

Choose a lead rider and a sweep rider, the most experienced riders. The leader looks ahead for changes in road, traffic or weather and signals early. The sweep rides last and sets the pace for the group.
Place inexperienced riders just behind the leader, so they do not have to chase the group and experienced riders can watch them.
Set route length and the pace through curves by the least experienced rider. If needed, split into two groups with different speeds.
Review the group hand signals at the rider's meeting so everyone can communicate on the road.
Take timely breaks to prevent loss of concentration and reduce fatigue.

rows: Arm and index finger extended straight up.
Arm extended straight up with index and middle fingers extended.
Arm extended straight down, palm facing back.
Arm straight out, palm up, swing upward.
Arm straight out, palm down, swing down to your side.
On the left, point with your left hand; on the right, point with your right foot.

blocks.text: The most important group rules: no competition, no passing other riders and no tailgating. Do not encourage the rider in front to speed. If someone insists on riding faster, let them go ahead to an agreed meeting point.

items: Check your mirrors to watch the rider behind you. If someone falls behind, everyone slows down to keep the group together.
Never ride side by side in the same lane. There is no room to steer around a car or hazard. Wait until you are stopped to talk.

blocks.text: Keep close ranks, but leave each rider enough space cushion to react to hazards. A close group takes up less road, is easier to see and is less likely to get separated. A staggered formation is the best way to do both.

rows: Right side of the lane, at least 1 second behind the leader.
Left side, at least 2 seconds behind the leader.
Right side, at least 2 seconds behind the second rider, and so on.

blocks.caption: Staggered formation: leader on the left, rider 2 on the right at least 1 second back, rider 3 on the left at least 2 seconds behind the leader.

items: Switch to single file in curves, when turning, and when entering or leaving freeways and highways.

Freeways: staggered formation is essential, but enter single file and form up only after everyone has merged. The leader moves the group over at least one lane, away from entering and exiting traffic. In heavy traffic, keep the 1-second and 2-second spacing. Exit single file.

Intersections are the highest-risk spot for a group. Left turn on a green arrow: tighten up and turn single file, never side by side. If the light changes before everyone gets through, those who made it stop at a safe point ahead and wait, so no one feels pushed to speed or run the red.
Parking: park together when you can, avoid parking downhill or head-in, and park so the group can leave as a unit in single file.

blocks.text: On a freeway or interstate the group may pass slow traffic as a unit. On a two-lane highway, riders in a staggered formation pass one at a time, and only where passing is allowed.

blocks.caption: Broken yellow center line: you may pass when it is safe.
Double solid yellow: no passing from either side.
Do Not Pass zone: wait until it ends.

items: The leader pulls out and passes when it is safe, with a clear view of oncoming traffic.
After passing, the leader returns to the left position and keeps riding at passing speed to open room for the next rider.
The second rider moves up to the left position and waits for their own safe chance. Conditions may have changed since the leader passed.
After passing, the second rider returns to the right position and opens room for the next rider. Each rider moves back into the same position held before the pass.

blocks.text: The leader should not move to the right side after passing. That can tempt the next rider to pass and cut in before there is enough space in front of the passed vehicle.

keyPoints: Only experienced riders should carry passengers or big loads; check both tires, the suspension and the headlight aim.
Passengers need matching protective gear, footrests and handholds; children sit right behind the rider.
Passengers mount after the engine is running in neutral, sit forward, hold on, keep feet on the pegs and lean with you.
With a passenger, ride slower in curves, start slowing earlier and keep a bigger space cushion.
Keep cargo low, balanced, over or ahead of the rear axle, and tied with multi-point elastic cords.
In a group, the most experienced lead and sweep, newer riders ride behind the leader, and no one competes, passes or tailgates.
Staggered formation: leader left, second right 1 second back, third left 2 seconds back; go single file in curves, turns and on ramps.
On two-lane roads pass one at a time, with the leader returning to the left position afterward.
